To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the pictorial structures formulation is a generic approach for both detection and articulated pose problems and (2) the selection of components for appearance and spatial modeling are crucial for general applicabilty and overall performance.

(i) shape context is an excellent appearance descriptor for body parts; (ii) discriminatively trained Ada-Boost classifiers are a good generative model of the shape context distribution, (iii) the normalized margin of a classifier is a good estimate of the likelihood of a part, (iv) the spatial relationships between parts should be represented as Gaussians, and (v) a pictorial structures model that combines these ingredients is an excellent generic model of people and their poses.

the pictorial structures model, if used in a principled manner, can handle a large range of problems in the area of articulated object detection, and that the performance can be significantly improved by a careful selection of components.
